content.thinking: I'm dropping the revision name from the root_cause field, and I want to double-check whether the still_at_risk mention of a revision is acceptable as it stands, since it may be fine. The root cause line is going to start with the deployed change rewriting things.

action_items.item: Add a check to io-shop's pipeline that times the account-page summary functions on accounts with long purchase histories and fails any change whose cost grows beyond a set bound.
Roll io-shop deployments out to a canary replica first, and hold the rollout while that replica's p95 latency is compared with replicas still on the earlier revision.
Route the HighLatency alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' requests to io-shop were answered far more slowly than usual, while no larger share of them failed than before.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1 of revision 70dbcfde2b549d110a3817d92d60b6dd9786e78b: the metrics read show the service healthy with it in place until the onset, and rolling back to it returned the service to normal, which was confirmed.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus.

causal_chain.step: Deploy P2 by kuki at {P2.1} put revision 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655 on io-shop, in the minute the onset was placed in. As of {T11.1}, all replicas ran that revision, so the slowdown was not a split between versions.

The revision rewrote average_spend_per_item, the function render_spend_summary calls for the account page's lifetime figure when neither rollout flag is set. It replaced dividing the account's carried total by its number of purchases with a loop that, for each purchase, re-sums the prices of every purchase up to that one.
Each call now did work that grows with the square of the shopper's purchase count instead of a single division, so pages that showed the figure took far longer to compute.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A software update changed how the shop works out a shopper's average spend per item: it now adds up the shopper's past purchases again for each purchase in turn, so the more a shopper had bought, the more work each page took.

contributing_factors.factor: No check of how long the account-page calculations take on a long purchase history was seen before the change went out. The tests at the revision check only correct values, on accounts with a handful of purchases.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check timing average_spend_per_item on a long history would have failed on the prefix-re-summing loop, and the revision would have been stopped before it reached production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No staged or canary rollout was seen: the revision reached every replica, with nothing seen comparing latency on new replicas against the earlier revision before the rollout completed.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The slowdown would have reached only part of the traffic and could have halted the rollout before every shopper's requests were slowed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read that every replica ran revision 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655, which tied the slowdown to that deploy and ruled out a split between versions.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else, which ruled out a flag as the trigger.
The Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed the rollback once the service was no longer at the incident's level.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #553 for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert fired but was not linked to an on-call incident, so no person was called in to the response.

input.root_cause: average_spend_per_item was rewritten so that, for every purchase in an account's history, it re-sums the prices of all purchases up to that point and keeps only the last pass. The work per call therefore grows with the square of the number of purchases, where before it was a single division of the account's carried total. render_spend_summary takes this path for the account page's figure whenever neither rollout flag is set.
input.still_at_risk: Revision 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655 still holds the slow calculation, and deploying it or anything built on it again would slow the shop's responses in the same way.
input.symptom: Shoppers' requests to the shop were answered far more slowly than usual
